title: dedicated: improve fleet autoscaler burst controls + utilization reporting (v7)
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: customers on Dedicated have been impacted by sudden workload spikes where short-lived bursts exhaust reserved GPU pools, causing request throttling and tail-latency spikes. Previous autoscaler iterations improved steady-state scaling but did not provide fine-grained per-fleet burst budgets and visibility. This PR implements a configurable burst control layer in the fleet autoscaler and significantly improves utilization reporting to help SREs and customers understand burst consumption and reclaimable capacity. Changes include: 1) an API and config surface for per-fleet burst budgets and token-bucket semantics; 2) a burst admission controller in the autoscaler that enforces burst budgets while preserving latency SLOs; 3) enhanced utilization metrics (burst_consumed, burst_remaining, utilization_by_instance_type, short_window_p95) and per-route breakdowns exposed to Redwood Console; 4) improved export of utilization reports to the reporting pipeline for historical analysis and billing reconciliation; 5) migration code to translate v5/v6 burst configs to the new token-bucket model. Testing and rollout: unit + integration tests added; staged canary rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleets, with automatic rollback on increased error rate or >10% unexpected throttle events. Backwards compatibility: existing burst flags remain supported for one release; cluster-level defaults applied when fleet config absent. See docs/ for config examples and migration notes.

review_comments: Lucas Kim (review): Can we ensure the new token-bucket window aligns with existing autoscaler evaluation windows? Suggest default of 60s to match short-window metrics.
Priya Shah (author): Updated default to 60s and added explicit note in docs. Also added a config override for fleets with sub-second SLA requirements.
Ana Rodriguez (review): Prometheus labels look good; please add per-instance-type cardinality guard to avoid high label cardinality in large customers.
Priya Shah (author): Added instance_type cardinality guard and unit tests to assert label limits.
ci_checks: benchmark-lab: pass (throughput neutral, 3% tail improvement under burst)
notes_on_tests: Integration harness includes a synthetic burst workload that exercises token-bucket exhaustion and recovery. Added deterministic clock to unit tests to avoid timing flakiness.
migration_notes: A migration path is provided: on startup, v5/v6 burst flags are translated to default token-bucket params. Admins can supply custom fleet configs to opt into stricter budgets. Migration is reversible until the next major config cleanup release.
release_notes:
- Added per-fleet burst budgets (token-bucket model) to control short-term spikes and protect reserved capacity
- Exposed burst_consumed and burst_remaining metrics in Console and Prometheus
- Improved utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets, including per-instance-type breakdowns
- Backwards-compatible migration from v5/v6 burst flags
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to 10% fleets for 48h, monitor dedicated_throttle_rate, request_error_rate, and burst_remaining metrics. If safe, ramp to 50% then 100% over 7 days. Automatic rollback on policy-triggered alarms.
changelog_summary: Introduce token-bucket burst controls and enrich Dedicated utilization telemetry to improve SLOs and observability for bursty workloads.
hotfix_followup: Added a follow-up hotfix scheduled (feature/hotfix/dedicated-burst-metrics-fix) to address an edge-case metric label emitted when instance_type is unknown; will be merged after canary.
